_note: Verification records for citations that CANNOT be machine-fetched, written and checked by experiments/audit_manual.py and asserted offline by tests/test_refs_manual.py. This is the OpenReview-shaped hole in the arXiv audit: audit_refs.py fetches arXiv abstract pages, but OpenReview serves a bot challenge on every endpoint, so an OpenReview citation could previously sit in a markdown bibliography behind a hand-typed '[unverified]' marker forever, with nothing recording whether anyone had actually read it. That is the F43 failure shape (a hand audit that misses one entry looks exactly like a hand audit that misses none) reintroduced in a file the arXiv machinery never covered. A record here carries EVIDENCE -- what was read, on what date, and the sha256 of the artifact -- so the check is reproducible and tamper-evident even though the fetch is not automatable.

_status_values.verified: the source was obtained and read; title/authors/venue below are transcribed from it
_status_values.unverified: not yet obtained; `reason` says why and `action` says what would close it

fundamental_limits_2026.title: On the Fundamental Limits of LLMs at Scale
fundamental_limits_2026.why_not_automated: OpenReview returns HTTP 403 ChallengeRequiredError on the forum page, the v1 and v2 note APIs, and the PDF endpoint. The challenge is a deliberate anti-automation measure and is not routed around.
fundamental_limits_2026.checked_against: local PDF obtained by the author through a browser; pages 1-10 and 13-18 read in full, including Table 1 (epistemic status of claims) and section 2.4 (creativity-factuality trade-off)
fundamental_limits_2026.pdf_location: held outside the repo (third-party PDF, not redistributed); the hash pins it wherever it is kept
fundamental_limits_2026.why_it_is_cited: Section 2.4 posits the creativity-factuality trade-off as A(theta) + alpha*C(theta) = kappa, giving dA = -alpha*dC -- a MONOTONE trade-off with constant alpha -- and its own Table 1 files this under 'modeling assumption / framework' rather than proved or empirical. Section 5.3 of assembly_theory.md measures exactly that, on a temperature grid spanning both of the regimes section 2.4 names (T ~ 0.1-0.5 repetitive, T ~ 1.0-2.0 hallucinating). F74 is the sharper contact: the paper's C is 'a creativity metric measuring diversity, novelty, or originality', and F74 measured twelve standard candidates for that metric, eleven of which peak on DEGENERATE REPETITION rather than on real text.
